cells.tense: Right now you're keeping the account, and the account is honest — what you owe and what's owed you both in view.
cells.verb: weighing what's fair without the scale tipping into your hands.
cells.place: in the pull toward what you actually want, where your own compass sets the direction.
cells.ask: offer to gather one thing this practice has grown — harvest the yield rather than judge it.
cells.core: You know what's right, and it doesn't cost you anything to know it. The weighing happens close to the bone but it stays clean — you can feel the difference between what you owe and what you're owed without either one running the room. That steadiness is what lets the pull toward what you want stay trustworthy: your compass is set, so the star can be followed. What this balance is free to feed next is the gathering — what the practice already grew, taken in hand.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair, and it doesn't cost you anything to know it.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead there's a reckoning you're already living in — every account balanced in advance, every wrong corrected before it lands.
cells.verb: auditing everyone's debts, including yours, before they've been incurred.
cells.place: in the pull toward what you actually want, which keeps getting checked against whether you deserve it.
cells.ask: lay down the ledger and hold what's yours without forcing it to come out even; strength shared is what steadies the scale, not more calculating.
cells.core: You're running the fairness ahead of the facts. Before anything has happened, you've already worked out what everyone should owe and what you'll be owed — and each time the pull toward what you want arrives, the arithmetic gets there first and asks whether you've earned it. The counting has taken the wheel, and the thing you actually want has become a claim you keep checking.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping accounts for things that haven't happened yet.

cells.tense: There was a moment the fairness went quiet — some door you closed on your own knowing, and you're still standing there.
cells.verb: holding back from what's yours to claim, the compass left unread.
cells.place: in the pull toward what you want, which you keep deferring as if wanting it were a debt you haven't earned.
cells.ask: let one practice be enough as it is — do it without improving anything, and let the solitude connect rather than audit.
cells.core: You stopped taking your own sense of what's right seriously. Not because you stopped having it — you can still feel the compass needle move — but somewhere back there, saying what you knew cost you more than staying quiet did. Now the pull toward what you want arrives and you treat it as a claim you don't have standing to make. The knowing hasn't gone anywhere. The standing up for it did.
cells.sheetLine: You still feel the compass, you've just stopped letting it point anywhere.

cells.tense: Right now you're keeping the account and calling it nothing — a mood, a tiredness, a settling of the air.
cells.verb: reading the compass and calling the reading just what's obvious.
cells.place: in the pull toward what you want, which is being steered by something you haven't named.
cells.ask: notice one thing you already know is right and stop calling it obvious — say it once as knowledge that's yours.
cells.core: Your sense of what's fair is running the room and you're not claiming it. You say no to things and call it just being practical; you know what should happen and describe it as what anyone would think. The compass is live — it's the one steering toward what matters — but the readout isn't yours. What you already know keeps arriving, clean and correct, and you keep filing it as something you happened to notice.
cells.sheetLine: You already know what's right. You just haven't called the knowing yours.
